This, to me, is the fundamental question we (and the mods) should seek to answer before we can truly consider proposed solutions such as those suggested by /u/chags in this comment.

For example:

  • /v/atheism is successful if it has a maximal effect on moving the largest number of people along the value chain: passive theist -> questioning theist -> confirmed atheist -> angry atheist -> contented atheist
  • /v/atheism is successful if it provides a recognized, respected social forum for atheists to intelligently discuss things related to atheism
  • /v/atheism is successful if it provides a recognized, respected social forum that materially contributes to the development of new ideas relevant to atheism
  • /v/atheism is successful if it maximizes the number of subscribers

When it comes to memes, I want to play devil's advocate: despite our collective distaste for the present incarnation of r/atheism, memes are materially useful if we assume the first of the above three. Compared to any other conveyance of an idea, the meme structure is superficial - the equivalent of a bumper sticker - but there is value in getting to the point quickly. Memes are a useful technology because they spread (atheistic) messages far/wide/quickly on social media. I have no evidence to support it, but I tend to think that that the widespread existence of atheistic memes, even dumb and offensive ones is a net positive. I think it creates more tailwinds (ie easier for more people to acknowledge themselves as atheist) than it does headwinds (making people on the fence more defensive about their theistic beliefs).

Therefore if the goal is to make more atheists happen, I think memes should be tolerated. But if the goal is to create a forum for existing atheists to engage in intellectual discussion, then mods should disallow image posts. A reliance on mod curation/deletion is not scalable.

Either way, I would encourage mods to consider any thoughts shared here in comments, and then to share their vision for what /v/atheism seeks to accomplish. And then to state this in the sidebar.
How do we define/measure the success of /v/atheism?
